author: Thomas à Kempis
title: With how great reverence Christ must be received

verses.text: The Voice of the Disciple
verses.modernizedText: The Voice of the Disciple

verses.text: These are Thy words, O Christ, Eternal Truth; though not uttered at one time nor written together in one place of Scripture.
verses.modernizedText: These are Your words, O Christ, Eternal Truth, though they were not spoken at one time or written together in one place in Scripture.

verses.text: Because therefore they are Thy words and true, I must gratefully and faithfully receive them all.
verses.modernizedText: Because they are Your words and true, I must receive them all gratefully and faithfully.

verses.text: They are Thine, and Thou hast uttered them; and they are mine also, because Thou didst speak them for my salvation.
verses.modernizedText: They are Yours, and You have spoken them; and they are mine also, because You spoke them for my salvation.

verses.text: Gladly I receive them from Thy mouth, that they may be more deeply implanted in my heart.
verses.modernizedText: Gladly I receive them from Your mouth, so that they may be planted more deeply in my heart.

verses.text: Words of such great grace arouse me, for they are full of sweetness and love; but my own sins terrify me, and my impure conscience driveth me away from receiving so great mysteries.
verses.modernizedText: Words of such great grace awaken me, for they are full of sweetness and love; but my own sins terrify me, and my impure conscience drives me away from receiving such great mysteries.

verses.text: The sweetness of Thy words encourageth me, but the multitude of my faults presseth me down.
verses.modernizedText: The sweetness of Your words encourages me, but the multitude of my faults presses me down.

verses.text: Thou commandest that I draw near to Thee with firm confidence, if I would have part with Thee, and that I receive the food of immortality, if I desire to obtain eternal life and glory.
verses.modernizedText: You command me to draw near to You with firm confidence if I would have a part with You, and to receive the food of immortality if I desire to obtain eternal life and glory.

verses.text: Come unto Me, sayest Thou, all that labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.
verses.modernizedText: Come to Me, You say, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

verses.text: Oh, sweet and lovely word in the ear of the sinner, that Thou, O Lord my God, dost invite the poor and needy to the Communion of Thy most holy body and blood.
verses.modernizedText: Oh, sweet and lovely word in the sinner’s ear, that You, O Lord my God, invite the poor and needy to the Communion of Your most holy body and blood.

verses.text: But who am I, O Lord, that I should presume to approach unto Thee?
verses.modernizedText: But who am I, O Lord, that I should presume to approach You?

verses.text: Behold the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee, and yet Thou sayest, Come ye all unto Me.
verses.modernizedText: See, the heaven of heavens cannot contain You, and yet You say, Come all of you to Me.

verses.text: What meaneth this most gracious condescension, this most lovely invitation?
verses.modernizedText: What does this most gracious condescension, this most lovely invitation mean?

verses.text: How shall I dare to come, who know no good thing of myself, whence I might be able to presume?
verses.modernizedText: How shall I dare to come, knowing no good thing of myself on which I might presume?

verses.text: How shall I bring Thee within my house, seeing that I so often have sinned in Thy most loving sight?
verses.modernizedText: How shall I bring You into my house, seeing that I have so often sinned in Your most loving sight?

verses.text: Angels and Archangels stand in awe of Thee, the Saints and just men fear Thee, and Thou sayest, Come unto Me!
verses.modernizedText: Angels and Archangels stand in awe of You, the Saints and just people fear You, and You say, Come to Me!

verses.text: Except Thou, Lord, hadst said it, who should believe it true?
verses.modernizedText: Unless You, Lord, had said it, who would believe it true?

verses.text: And except Thou hadst commanded, who should attempt to draw near?
verses.modernizedText: And unless You had commanded it, who would attempt to draw near?

verses.text: Behold, Noah, that just man, laboured for a hundred years in building the ark, that he might be saved with the few; and I, how shall I be able in one hour to prepare myself to receive the Builder of the world with reverence?
verses.modernizedText: See, Noah, that just man, labored for a hundred years building the ark so that he might be saved with the few; and how shall I be able in one hour to prepare myself to receive the Builder of the world with reverence?

verses.text: Moses, Thy servant, Thy great and especial friend, made an ark of incorruptible wood, which also he covered with purest gold, that he might lay up in it the tables of the law, and I, a corruptible creature, shall I dare thus easily to receive Thee, the Maker of the Law and the Giver of life?
verses.modernizedText: Moses, Your servant, Your great and special friend, made an ark of incorruptible wood, which he covered with the purest gold so that he might store in it the tablets of the law; and shall I, a corruptible creature, dare so easily to receive You, the Maker of the Law and the Giver of life?

verses.text: Solomon, the wisest of the kings of Israel, was seven years building his magnificent temple to the praise of Thy Name, and for eight days celebrated the feast of its dedication, offered a thousand peace offerings, and solemnly brought up the Ark of the Covenant to the place prepared for it, with the sound of trumpets and great joy, and I, unhappy and poorest of mankind, how shall I bring Thee into my house, who scarce know how to spend half an hour in devotion?
verses.modernizedText: Solomon, the wisest of the kings of Israel, spent seven years building his magnificent temple to the praise of Your Name, and for eight days celebrated the feast of its dedication, offered a thousand peace offerings, and solemnly brought the Ark of the Covenant to the place prepared for it, with the sound of trumpets and great joy. And how shall I, unhappy and poorest of humankind, bring You into my house, when I scarcely know how to spend half an hour in devotion?

verses.text: And oh that it were even one half hour worthily spent!
verses.modernizedText: And oh, that even one half hour were worthily spent!

verses.text: O my God, how earnestly these holy men strove to please Thee!
verses.modernizedText: O my God, how earnestly these holy people strove to please You!

verses.text: And alas! how little and trifling is that which I do! how short a time do I spend, when I am disposing myself to Communion.
verses.modernizedText: And alas, how little and trifling is what I do! How short a time I spend preparing myself for Communion.

verses.text: Rarely altogether collected, most rarely cleansed from all distraction.
verses.modernizedText: Rarely am I entirely collected, and most rarely cleansed from all distraction.

verses.text: And surely in the saving presence of Thy Godhead no unmeet thought ought to intrude, nor should any creature take possession of me, because it is not an Angel but the Lord of the Angels, that I am about to receive as my Guest.
verses.modernizedText: And surely in the saving presence of Your Godhead no unworthy thought ought to intrude, nor should any creature take possession of me, because it is not an Angel but the Lord of the Angels whom I am about to receive as my Guest.

verses.text: Yet there is a vast difference between the Ark of the Covenant with its relics, and Thy most pure Body with its ineffable virtues, between those sacrifices of the law, which were figures of things to come, and the true sacrifice of Thy Body, the completion of all the ancient sacrifices.
verses.modernizedText: Yet there is a vast difference between the Ark of the Covenant with its relics and Your most pure Body with its unspeakable virtues, between those sacrifices of the law, which were figures of things to come, and the true sacrifice of Your Body, the completion of all the ancient sacrifices.

verses.text: Wherefore then do I not yearn more ardently after Thy adorable presence?
verses.modernizedText: Why then do I not yearn more ardently for Your adorable presence?

verses.text: Why do I not prepare myself with greater solicitude to receive Thy holy things, when those holy Patriarchs and Prophets of old, kings also and princes, with the whole people, manifested so great affection of devotion towards Thy Divine Service?
verses.modernizedText: Why do I not prepare myself with greater care to receive Your holy things, when those holy Patriarchs and Prophets of old, kings and princes also, with the whole people, showed such great affection of devotion toward Your Divine Service?

verses.text: The most devout king David danced with all his might before the Ark of God, calling to mind the benefits granted to his forefathers in days past; he fashioned musical instruments of various sorts, put forth Psalms, and appointed them to be sung with joy, played also himself ofttimes on the harp, being inspired with the grace of the Holy Ghost; he taught the people of Israel to praise God with the whole heart, and with unity of voice to bless and praise Him every day.
verses.modernizedText: The most devout king David danced with all his might before the Ark of God, recalling the benefits granted to his ancestors in days past. He made musical instruments of various kinds, composed Psalms and appointed them to be sung with joy; he also often played the harp himself, inspired by the grace of the Holy Spirit. He taught the people of Israel to praise God with their whole heart and with one voice to bless and praise Him every day.

verses.text: If so great devotion was then exercised, and celebration of divine praise was carried on before the Ark of the Testimony, how great reverence and devotion ought now to be shown by me and all Christian people at the ministering of the Sacrament, at receiving the most precious Body and Blood of Christ.
verses.modernizedText: If such great devotion was then practiced, and divine praise celebrated before the Ark of the Testimony, how great a reverence and devotion ought now to be shown by me and all Christian people at the ministering of the Sacrament, at receiving the most precious Body and Blood of Christ.

verses.text: Many run to diverse places to visit the memorials of departed Saints, and rejoice to hear of their deeds and to look upon the beautiful buildings of their shrines.
verses.modernizedText: Many run to various places to visit memorials of departed Saints, and rejoice to hear of their deeds and look upon the beautiful buildings of their shrines.

verses.text: And behold, Thou art present here with me, O my God, Saint of Saints, Creator of men and Lord of the Angels.
verses.modernizedText: And see, You are present here with me, O my God, Saint of Saints, Creator of people and Lord of the Angels.

verses.text: Often in looking at those memorials men are moved by curiosity and novelty, and very little fruit of amendment is borne away, especially when there is so much careless trifling and so little true contrition.
verses.modernizedText: Often in looking at those memorials people are moved by curiosity and novelty, and carry away very little fruit of amendment, especially when there is so much careless trifling and so little true contrition.

verses.text: But here in the Sacrament of the Altar, Thou art present altogether, My God, the Man Christ Jesus; where also abundant fruit of eternal life is given to every one soever that receiveth Thee worthily and devoutly.
verses.modernizedText: But here in the Sacrament of the Altar, You are altogether present, my God, the Man Christ Jesus; and here abundant fruit of eternal life is given to everyone who receives You worthily and devoutly.

verses.text: But to this no levity draweth, no curiosity, nor sensuality, only steadfast faith, devout hope, and sincere charity.
verses.modernizedText: But no frivolity, curiosity, or sensuality draws anyone to this, only steadfast faith, devout hope, and sincere charity.

verses.text: O God, invisible Creator of the world, how wondrously dost Thou work with us, how sweetly and graciously Thou dealest with Thine elect, to whom Thou offerest Thyself to be received in this Sacrament!
verses.modernizedText: O God, invisible Creator of the world, how wonderfully You work with us, how sweetly and graciously You deal with Your elect, to whom You offer Yourself to be received in this Sacrament!

verses.text: For this surpasseth all understanding, this specially draweth the hearts of the devout and enkindleth their affections.
verses.modernizedText: For this surpasses all understanding; it especially draws the hearts of the devout and kindles their affections.

verses.text: For even thy true faithful ones themselves, who order their whole life to amendment, oftentimes gain from this most excellent Sacrament great grace of devotion and love of virtue.
verses.modernizedText: For even Your true faithful ones themselves, who order their whole life toward amendment, often gain from this most excellent Sacrament great grace of devotion and love of virtue.

verses.text: Oh admirable and hidden grace of the Sacrament, which only Christ’s faithful ones know, but the faithless and those who serve sin cannot experience!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, admirable and hidden grace of the Sacrament, which only Christ’s faithful ones know, but which the faithless and those who serve sin cannot experience!

verses.text: In this Sacrament is conferred spiritual grace, and lost virtue is regained in the soul, and the beauty which was disfigured by sin returneth again.
verses.modernizedText: In this Sacrament spiritual grace is conferred, lost virtue is regained in the soul, and the beauty disfigured by sin returns again.

verses.text: So great sometimes is this grace that out of the fulness of devotion given, not only the mind but also the weak body feeleth that more strength is supplied unto it.
verses.modernizedText: Sometimes this grace is so great that from the fullness of devotion given, not only the mind but also the weak body feels that more strength is supplied to it.

verses.text: But greatly must we mourn and lament over our lukewarmness and negligence, that we are not drawn by greater affection to become partakers of Christ, in whom all the hope and the merit of those that are to be saved consist.
verses.modernizedText: But we must greatly mourn and lament our lukewarmness and negligence, that we are not drawn with greater affection to become partakers of Christ, in whom all the hope and merit of those who are to be saved consist.

verses.text: For He Himself is our sanctification and redemption.(1) He is the consolation of pilgrims and the eternal fruition of the Saints.
verses.modernizedText: For He Himself is our sanctification and redemption.(1) He is the consolation of pilgrims and the eternal enjoyment of the Saints.

verses.text: Therefore it is grievously to be lamented that many so little consider this health-giving mystery, which maketh heaven glad and preserveth the whole world.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore it is greatly to be lamented that many give so little thought to this health-giving mystery, which makes heaven glad and preserves the whole world.

verses.text: Alas for the blindness and hardness of man’s heart, that he considereth not more this unspeakable gift, and even slippeth down through the daily use, into carelessness.
verses.modernizedText: Alas for the blindness and hardness of the human heart, that one does not consider this unspeakable gift more and even slips into carelessness through daily use.

verses.text: For if this most holy Sacrament were celebrated in one place only, and were consecrated only by one priest in the whole world, with what great desire thinkest thou, would men be affected towards that place and towards such a priest of God, that they might behold the divine mysteries celebrated?
verses.modernizedText: For if this most holy Sacrament were celebrated in only one place and consecrated by only one priest in the whole world, with what great desire do you think people would be drawn to that place and that priest of God, so that they might see the divine mysteries celebrated?

verses.text: But now are many men made priests and in many places the Sacrament is celebrated, that the grace and love of God towards men might the more appear, the more widely the Holy Communion is spread abroad over all the world.
verses.modernizedText: But now many are made priests and the Sacrament is celebrated in many places, so that the grace and love of God toward people might appear all the more as Holy Communion is spread more widely over all the world.

verses.text: Thanks be unto Thee, O good Jesus, Eternal Shepherd, who hast vouchsafed to refresh us, poor and exiled ones, with Thy precious Body and Blood, and to invite us to partake these holy mysteries by the invitation from Thine own mouth, saying, Come unto Me, ye who labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.
verses.modernizedText: Thanks be to You, O good Jesus, Eternal Shepherd, who have graciously refreshed us, poor and exiled ones, with Your precious Body and Blood, and invited us to partake of these holy mysteries by the invitation from Your own mouth, saying, Come to Me, you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.
